checks.name: Forwarding only
checks.output: 2 tests pass. Resolving AUTOMONIQUE_DB yields SpellingResolution::Canonical and resolving LEGACY_DB yields SpellingResolution::Alias, and both hand back the same NameEntry: identical canonical(), owner() and durable_identity(). An unknown spelling yields SpellingResolution::Unknown. LegacyAlias has exactly three fields (spelling, authorized_by, retire_after) and no behavior-carrying field or method, so an alias can only forward; a codec boundary is permitted by the contract but none is represented here, which is consistent with "forwarding or codec".

checks.name: Conflict rejection
checks.output: 3 tests pass. Setting AUTOMONIQUE_DB=/new and LEGACY_DB=/old returns CompatError::CanonicalAndAliasBothSet naming both spellings and both values; the rendered message contains /new, /old and the word "precedence". Reversing declaration order gives the same category and still names both values. Two identical values under both spellings are still an error, so agreeing by accident is not tolerated. resolve_configuration has no precedence branch: every duplicate canonical target returns Err.

checks.name: Deprecation observation
